messages:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: Pager: auth-proxy-01 reported sustained anomalous traffic pattern -> 401 spike from multiple IPs and several leaked debug log entries forwarded to external bucket. Severity: P1. Bridge: https://meet.redwood/incident/6198765432
Amanda S: Ack. I'm oncall. Opening the bridge now.
Amanda S: Quick ask — any customer-facing errors? telemetry shows a bump in 401s for the embed endpoint, ~0.8% of requests in the last 10m.
Sanjay P: Confirmed, dashboards: `auth.proxy.401_rate` jumped x12. A few log lines contain truncated auth headers (token fragments). Sample: `2026-03-18T17:07:02Z proxy auth failed src=3.8.12.45 token=eyJhbG...X9a`
Maria L: :eyes: That token snippet looks like a real service token. Checking whether it's from a staging forwarder or prod. Giving me 2m.
infra-bot: s3-notifier: external-bucket `public-uploads-logs` received recent upload `auth-2026-03-18-17-05.json.gz` from user agent `logshipper/1.2`.
Amanda S: Ok — action items: (1) Sanjay, confirm whether uploads contain PII or full tokens. (2) Kevin, prepare emergency rotation plan for the proxied service account and any affected client tokens. (3) Maria, start a quick forensics of the s3 object and IPs. I'll loop in Legal.
Kevin R: On it. If tokens are valid we rotate svcacct immediately and revoke session cookies. Will prepare rotation script. Potential user impact: active sessions may get logged out ~10-15m during rotation.
Sanjay P: I'm tailing the upload. It looks like the file contains debug traces with full `Authorization` headers for ~7k requests. IPs include `3.8.12.45` and `54.23.11.90` (both external). Not internal-aws.
Maria L: Forensics: the uploader used an ephemeral CI key associated with a stale deploy job. Looks like a misconfigured forwarder in staging that pointed at prod bucket name. Evidence: `CI_JOB_ID=4021` in file headers.
Amanda S: That narrows it. Decision: treat as data exposure. Triggering key rotation for the service account used by the forwarder and revoking the CI job token. Also schedule immediate S3 object quarantine.
Legal Team: We need timestamped preservation of current evidence and a short customer notification draft. Keep chain-of-custody notes in the bridge.
infra-bot: action: quarantining s3 object `public-uploads-logs/auth-2026-03-18-17-05.json.gz` -> moving to `s3://redwood-incidents/quarantine/6198765432/`
Amanda S: Kevin, post rotation commands here when ready. Include any temporary mitigation (WAF rule) if rotation takes >10m.
Kevin R: Rotation plan (short): 1) create replacement keys in KMS for `svc-forwarder-prod`; 2) update forwarder role binding to new key; 3) revoke old key and invalidate tokens (IAM revoke-session for linked tokens). Quick commands: `aws iam create-access-key --user svc-forwarder-prod` then deploy.
Sanjay P: While Kev rotates, I recommend a short-term rate block on the suspicious IPs plus a quick denylist for any public logshipper user agents. Adds protection while we rotate.
Maria L: Confirmed uploader CI job ID belongs to a partner repo. I'm DM'ing partner contact now.
Amanda S: Customer impact assessment: Embeddings and chat-throughput may see transient 401s for sessions tied to the forwarder config. Majority of customers unaffected, estimated <1% error surface. We should prepare a brief notification to customers in affected orgs.
Legal Team: Drafting customer notification: short, factual, and asking impacted orgs to rotate their keys if they pulled that artifact. Will post for review in 10m.
Amanda S: Sanjay, once you validate the quarantined object, please snapshot MD5 and add to evidence. Maria, capture the CI job and reproduce steps to prevent recurrence.
Sanjay P: Quarantined object MD5: `d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e`. Saved to incident doc.
infra-bot: IAM revoke issued for `AKIA...oldkey` and `session-ids` related.
Kevin R: New keys live and propagated to canary. Starting role swap now.I'll post rollback plan if anything breaks.
Amanda S: Good. Ops checklist: 1) quarantine object (done). 2) rotate keys (in progress). 3) WAF denylist (in progress). 4) revoke CI job and notify partner (in progress). 5) Legal/customer comms (in progress). 6) postmortem owner? @Sanjay P volunteer?
Sanjay P: I'll own postmortem.
Maria L: Partner responded — forwarder deploy was accidental; they are rotating their side keys and will pause CI jobs.
Amanda S: Any blockers on rotation?
Kevin R: No blockers. Canary passed. Proceeding to revoke old keys in 2m.
Amanda S: Rotation done. Old keys revoked. I see auth 401 spike dropping back toward baseline over the last 5m.
Sanjay P: Confirmed: 401 rate down to x1.3 baseline. No evidence tokens were used to access PII buckets. Access attempts from suspect IPs were limited to the embed endpoint only.
Legal Team: Final note — preserve quarantine and forensic snapshots for 12 months. Draft customer note ready: "We detected an exposure of debug logs from a misconfigured forwarder which contained truncated auth headers. We rotated affected keys and quarantined the logs. We do not believe customer data was accessed. Actions taken and recommended next steps..."
Amanda S: Closing actions: Sanjay to run postmortem, Maria to add CI forwarder guardrails (prevent prod bucket name usage), Kevin to add rotation automation for ephemeral CI creds. Legal to finalize notice. We'll update customers if partner confirms any exfil.
Amanda S: Incident DECLARED resolved at 2026-03-18T17:17:40Z :white_check_mark: Please file RCA in /incidents/6198765432-rca and link to this thread.
Kevin R: Noted. Pushing RFC for automated rotation.
Sanjay P: Postmortem ticket created: INC-6198765432. Assigned to me.
Maria L: I'll follow up with partner integration ticket.
pagerbot: Incident closed by Amanda S at 2026-03-18T17:17:40Z.
